QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_26

question.text: Ms. Anita Kapoor, LP in 'Mumbai Category II AIF', has a side-letter with a 'Most Favoured Nation' (MFN) provision. This entitles her to:

answer.text: Elect the benefit of rights contained in other investors' side-letters (and potentially also the right to view those side-letters)
First access to any new scheme launched by the Sponsor

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes an MFN provision as entitling the investor to elect the benefit of rights granted to other investors in their side-letters, and potentially the right to view those side-letters. The workbook also stresses that MFN usage in side-letters should be regularised. The Trap: A veto on investment decisions sits with the Investment Committee, not with an LP MFN. A "first access" capacity right and a guaranteed return are different concepts and are not how the workbook defines MFN. Note: The workbook addresses MFN on pages 235-236 and in the side-letter footnote on page 182; it does not prescribe threshold-based MFN tiering.
